clue.text: Easy for Barrie to write "Peter Pan "?

definitions.meaning: something very easy to do is said to be no harder than a youngster's game
J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan is a stage play written for youngsters

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a trivially simple task, and also literally a stage drama for youngsters, which is what Barrie's Peter Pan was.

clue.text: Their eyes are on the road

definitions.text: Their eyes are on the road

parts.words: Their eyes are on the road
parts.note: reflective road studs are named after the eyes of a household pet

explanation.definitionFit: Road reflectors are called by the name of these animals' eyes, which shine in headlights.

clue.text: Give O.k. sign to an amendment

definitions.text: Give O.k. sign to an amendment

parts.words: Give O.k. sign to an amendment
parts.note: to approve a change by writing one's own first letters beside it

explanation.definitionFit: To approve a change in a document by writing one's first letters next to it.

clue.text: Varden's contribution to cricket ?

parts.note: Dolly Varden is a character in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge, and in cricket a very easy chance to take is a 'dolly'

explanation.walkthrough: Dolly Varden is the flirtatious girl in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge; in cricket an easy catch is a 'dolly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple chances for a fielder in cricket, called dollies, credited here to Dickens's Dolly Varden.

clue.text: Tools-the best going to revolutionary centres

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best
an axis is the centre line something revolves around

explanation.surface: The finest instruments go to rebel leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests rebels; here it means turning, so the centres are axes of rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy digging implements with pointed iron heads.

clue.text: Shrewd, like a note containing disapproval .

indicators.note: containing means the note and 'like' hold the sound of disapproval between them

parts.note: as means like
E is a musical note
tut is a sound of disapproval

explanation.surface: Clever, like a memo with a scolding in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' gives a short connective, 'a note' one letter of the scale, and 'containing' means those two hold the sound of disapproval between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and sharp-witted are synonyms for being quick to see an advantage.

clue.text: Clique or cleek ?

definitions.meaning: a clique is an exclusive social set, like a members' society
a cleek is an old iron-headed golf stick

explanation.definitionFit: A clique is an exclusive circle of members, and a cleek is an old name for a particular golfing iron.

clue.text: Luxury animals

parts.note: small pampered pets kept for company, which sit on their owners' knees

explanation.definitionFit: Pampered pet dogs kept for comfort and sitting on a knee rather than for work.

clue.text: Don't give a straight talk (use these ?)

definitions.text: Don't give a straight talk (use these ?)

parts.words: Don't give a straight talk (use these ?)
parts.note: to argue back and forth is to bandy remarks, and bandy legs are not straight

explanation.definitionFit: To bandy remarks is to swap them in argument, and bandy also means bowed, not straight.

clue.text: The third form copy this

parts.note: a document made in three copies is in this form, the third copy being one of the set

explanation.definitionFit: Something made in threefold copies is in this form; the word means 'in three identical copies'.

clue.text: Cycle ride is one way to get around

definitions.meaning: a short ride for pleasure, on a bicycle or in a car, is a whirl round the lanes
to rotate or whirl is to turn around on the spot

explanation.surface: A bike outing is one way of getting about town.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pleasure ride is a 'spin' in British usage, and rotating means turning round about an axis.

clue.text: Banking arrangement necessary to pay the meat bill ?

definitions.text: Banking arrangement necessary to pay the meat bill ?

parts.words: Banking arrangement necessary to pay the meat bill ?
parts.note: a bank account shared by two people, read as a bill for a cut of meat from the butcher

explanation.definitionFit: A shared bank account, read playfully as the butcher's bill for a roast.

clue.text: Tunefully ethereal ?

parts.note: a word meaning light and ethereal which also suggests 'like a tune', since a tune is an air

explanation.definitionFit: Light and insubstantial, and also, by its root, full of tunes, since a melody is called an air.

clue.text: Subject requiring a lot of looking up

definitions.text: Subject requiring a lot of looking up

parts.words: Subject requiring a lot of looking up
parts.note: looking up here is gazing skyward at the stars, not consulting reference books

explanation.definitionFit: The science of stars and planets demands much gazing at the night sky.

clue.text: Lift chutes adapted for molluscs

definitions.note: the answer is the same in the plural

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Lifts and chutes modified to carry shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten-armed sea creatures with an internal shell, which are molluscs.

clue.text: Duel a don arranged without charge

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of these three words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A fellow at a college sets up a duel with pistols that hold no bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles DUELADON. 'charge' looks like a fee, but here it is the powder and shot in a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with no charge in it has had its ammunition removed.

clue.text: Remarkable for Scotland to have two quarters in this organization

indicators.note: in places the compass letters inside the Scots word

parts.note: unco is a Scots word meaning remarkable or extraordinary
E and S are east and south, two of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Scotland gets two of its regions represented in some notable body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Scotland' says the synonym of 'Remarkable' is a Scots word, and 'in' tells you the compass points go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization is a well-known international body.

clue.text: Rank Heather among the best going to court, though a tender plant

parts.note: to seed players is to rank them, as with the best tennis players going on court
ling is a name for heather

explanation.surface: A player named Heather is ranked among the top players at Wimbledon, though fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a name; it is LING. 'among the best going to court' describes seeding in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A young plant grown from seed, still delicate.

clue.text: Old Third Row church

parts.note: a row of seats is a tier
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A third row of pews in an ancient church.
explanation.walkthrough: The old word means a third: the third canonical hour of prayer, or the third fencing position.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a third part, still used for the third canonical hour and a fencing parry.

clue.text: Eastern politician bound to to be exhausted .

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
tied means bound

explanation.surface: An Eastern politician is sure to be worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' looks like 'certain to'; here 'bound' means tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank that is exhausted has been drained of all its contents.

clue.text: Docked and gave full particulars?

definitions.meaning: docked means had the tail cut off
gave every point of the account in full

explanation.surface: Someone arriving in port then explains everything at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Docked, read as having its tail cut off, and the ordinary verb for itemising fully.

clue.text: Descent of eagle in disarray

indicators.note: disarray means the letters of the two words are put in confusion

explanation.surface: An eagle tumbling down in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder; 'disarray' rearranges EAGLEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent, meaning ancestry or family line.

clue.text: This plane is not physical; like the R.A.F. goal

definitions.meaning: in occult belief the plane of existence beyond the physical is named after the stars
the RAF motto is 'per ardua ad astra', through adversity to the stars

explanation.surface: A spiritual realm likened to where the Royal Air Force aims.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Air Force's motto is 'Per ardua ad astra', 'through hardship to the stars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the stars, and the occult name for a spiritual plane beyond the physical.

clue.text: Spoke hastily ?

parts.note: the verb for putting words out also reads as 'sent by fast service', as with a fast train or letter

explanation.definitionFit: Put into words, and also, read playfully, sent by a fast delivery service.

clue.text: An inclination to hypocrisy

explanation.surface: Someone has a leaning towards saying what they do not mean.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt or slope, and also sanctimonious, insincere talk.

clue.text: See 28.

annotationWithheld.why: See 28. — a cross-reference: 28 & 25 together are one answer clued at 28-across, but the file holds no group, so 28-across holds the clue and this light has none of its own

clue.text: In the same place is found a bird

parts.note: ib. is the short form of ibidem, Latin for in the same place
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is always spotted at the same spot.
explanation.walkthrough: IB (ibidem, used in footnotes) plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading bird, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: A retail cut could come from this, that's clear

indicators.note: says that the clue's three words are a rearrangement of the answer's letters

explanation.surface: A shop's price reduction is easy to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs backwards: rearranging the answer gives A RETAIL CUT, so 'could come from this' points at the answer as the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear, well-expressed speech or writing is said to be fluent and lucid.

clue.text: Man-hunt in 1 Across (4 & 4).

parts.note: a game for youngsters in which one player searches for the others who have concealed themselves

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 28 and down 25, and 1 Across is CHILD'S PLAY, so this is a children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game of concealment and searching, in effect a small manhunt.

clue.text: Floor of a landing-craft, mainly ?

parts.note: the landing craft is an aircraft carrier, landing planes out on the main, the open sea

explanation.definitionFit: The deck of an aircraft carrier on which planes take off and touch down.
